Maria: quick heads-up — ran a weight-only (bitsandbytes / llm.int8) bakeoff on llama-3-7b today, and something odd popped up. throughput +2.7x vs fp16, but we're seeing a reproducible QC spike in hallucinations for high-temp sampling (temp >= 0.8).
Devin: paste the run and the eval numbers?
Maria: sure:
```
# convert + run
python convert.py --model llama-3-7b --format bnb --quantize int8
python bench.py --model ./bnb/llama-3-7b --batch 8 --seq 512 --temp 0.9 --samples 500
```
metrics: PPL fp16=12.4, int8=12.9; rouge-l drop ~1.8%; EM drop ~2.1% on our QA set; throughput fp16=80 tok/s, int8=216 tok/s.
Arjun: interesting. small perf/quality tradeoff is expected, but the temp sensitivity suggests decoding noise not just score shift. did you check layernorm/attention cast points? llm.int8 keeps some ops in fp32/fp16; folding mismatch can amplify sampling variance.
Maria: I dumped activations for a few failing prompts — top-k token probs are spikier under int8, and the next-token entropy lower (weird). also saw occasional repeated fragments at higher temps.
Zoe: we saw similar with AWQ on a different model: repeats and hallucinations clustered when the final transformer block used int8 kernels. patching last N layers to run in fp16 fixed it. tried last-2-layer-fp16?
Maria: tried last-3-layer-fp16 and reran. new metrics: PPL int8-last3fp16=12.55, rouge-l loss down to 0.7%, EM down to 0.6%. throughput dropped to 190 tok/s but still +2.3x over fp16.
Devin: nice. do we have a reproducible micro-batch that triggers the artifact so we can add an eval test?
Maria: yes — attaching a 5-example seed set in the ticket. examples usually have long context with list-of-steps -> model starts inventing extra steps under int8.
Arjun: likely root cause = quantization noise amplification in residual branch when final-layer matmuls are quantized. options: last-layer-fp16, per-channel scaling tweak, or small calibration (min-max vs MSE) on those layers. bitsandbytes has per-channel quantization flags we can try.
Zoe: also try lowering temp or using top-p at sample-time as a mitigation for hosted profiles. for Dedicated/Private we should add a deployment flag that forces last-N layers in fp16 for safety.
Maria: raising a tiny RFC -> add profile flag `int8_safe_tail_layers` with default 0; experiments suggest 2-3 is sweet spot for L3-7b. I'll open PR with bench script and example seeds.
eval-bot: automated regression check queued for PR #2367 — note: baseline is fp16 run from 2025-11-12.
Devin: action items: 1) PR for profile flag + docs, 2) add seedset to regression suite, 3) try bitsandbytes per-channel quant config and AWQ fallback.
Maria: yep. I'll draft PR and drop the seedset in /datasets/eval/llama3/int8_hallucination_seeds.json. tagging @arjun for review on the quantization theory bits. :rocket:
